reply_text:
I found five dated statements from 2015, plus three undated lines about when superhuman AI would arrive. All of the quotes were read on pages I opened. The best sources are Altman's own two-part blog essay "Machine intelligence" and Steven Levy's Q&A interview at the OpenAI launch. The self-driving-car forecast exists only as a TechCrunch paraphrase, not as his own words.

- **Dates of the blog posts:** neither page I opened shows a posting date. They are dated 2015 here because a LessWrong repost calls them "Sam Altman's 2015 Blog Posts." Many people cite them as February 25 and March 2, 2015, but I did not confirm that on a page.
- **Self-driving cars:** the "three to four years" figure is TechCrunch's paraphrase, not a direct quote. "He thought we'd see them in three to four years", at the Vanity Fair New Establishment Summit on Oct. 6, 2015, in San Francisco.
- **Borderline items:** the "multi-decade project" line answers a funding question ("Over what period of time?"), so you may decide it is a spending forecast and drop it. The "next century" line is rhetorical, and I kept it only because it names a span.
- **Left out:** the well-known June 2015 Airbnb Open Air line ("AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world…") gives no date. It is also not about when superhuman AI arrives, and I never opened the original Business Insider report, so it is not in the list.
- **Budget:** I used 11 of 12 searches and 5 of 6 page openings. One opening returned an error and is counted. The first search's results printed only partly because of a bug in my code; I fixed the code without running that search again.
